title: The UK Quiz
blurb: Britain from Scotland to Cornwall: places, history and culture.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Scotland?
questions.fact: Edinburgh Castle sits on an extinct volcano.

questions.q: What is the longest river in the UK?
questions.fact: The Severn is about 220 miles long.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain in the UK?
questions.fact: Ben Nevis in Scotland is 1,345 metres high.

questions.q: Who was the UK's first female Prime Minister?
questions.fact: She took office in 1979.

questions.q: In which year did the Great Fire of London happen?
questions.fact: It began in a baker's shop in Pudding Lane.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Wales?
questions.fact: Cardiff became the capital in 1955.

questions.q: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in which tower?
questions.fact: The tower was renamed in 2012 for the Queen's Diamond Jubilee.

questions.q: What is the national flower of England?
questions.fact: The red Tudor rose is the symbol of England.

questions.q: Which king of England had six wives?
questions.fact: Two of his wives were beheaded.

questions.q: Which city is home to Anfield stadium?
questions.fact: Anfield is home to Liverpool Football Club.

questions.q: Who wrote the Harry Potter books?
questions.fact: The first book came out in 1997.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Northern Ireland?
questions.fact: The Titanic was built in Belfast.

questions.q: Which batter-based side dish is traditionally served with a roast beef dinner?
questions.fact: A good Yorkshire pudding should rise high in a hot oven.

questions.q: Which London bridge has towers and can open to let ships through?
questions.fact: Its two halves lift up like drawbridges.

questions.q: Which two countries does the Channel Tunnel connect?
questions.fact: It opened in 1994 and trains take about 35 minutes to cross.

questions.q: In which school's playing fields was rugby supposedly invented?
questions.fact: The story says William Webb Ellis picked up the ball in 1823.

questions.q: What does BBC stand for?
questions.fact: The BBC began radio broadcasts in 1922.

questions.q: Which author created Sherlock Holmes?
questions.fact: Holmes lives at 221B Baker Street.

questions.q: What is the largest city in Scotland?
questions.fact: Glasgow is home to over 600,000 people.

questions.q: What is the name of the famous prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire?
questions.fact: Parts of Stonehenge are around 5,000 years old.

questions.q: Which year did England's men win the FIFA World Cup?
questions.fact: England beat West Germany 4-2 at Wembley.

questions.q: Which famous street in London is the home of the Prime Minister?
questions.fact: The Prime Minister lives at number 10.

questions.q: Who wrote 'On the Origin of Species'?
questions.fact: It was published in 1859.

questions.q: In which country is Loch Ness?
questions.fact: It is the largest lake in Britain by volume.

questions.q: How many countries make up the United Kingdom?
questions.fact: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

questions.q: Which UK city is nicknamed the 'Steel City'?
questions.fact: Sheffield was famous for making steel and cutlery.

questions.q: Which palace is the London home of the monarch?
questions.fact: It has 775 rooms.

questions.q: What is the UK's currency called?
questions.fact: The pound is the oldest currency still in use today.

questions.q: Which seaside city has a famous pier and a Pavilion known for its Indian-style domes?
questions.fact: The Royal Pavilion was built for the Prince Regent.
